fields.description: The master on/off switch. When it is off, nothing is profiled at all, even if people have sessions running. Use it to pause profiling across the whole site without changing anyone's individual widget.
fields.label: Profiler Enabled

fields.description: Optimus Session records older than this many days become eligible for the daily cleanup job to delete. Set it to 0 to keep them forever (the daily cleanup then does nothing). Reference values: Strict: 1  ·  Recommended: 30  ·  Relaxed: 7.
fields.label: Session Retention (days)

fields.options:
Tracked Apps is an allowlist when populated, only those apps' findings are actionable; everything else routes to Framework-level observations. Leave it empty to keep the default (frappe / erpnext / hrms / lms / helpdesk / insights / crm / builder / wiki / drive / payments and pip libs are treated as framework code).

Do not add frappe or erpnext to Tracked Apps. Doing so flips them to "user code" and floods your actionable findings with framework noise the opposite of what most users want. If you want them gone, add them to Ignored Apps (right) instead.

Ignored Apps is an exclusion list findings whose blame app falls in this list are dropped from the report entirely (both the "Findings what to fix" and "Framework-level observations" sections). Use it for apps you can't (or won't) patch. Default on fresh install: every Frappe-organization-maintained app is seeded frappe, erpnext, hrms, lms, helpdesk, insights, crm, builder, wiki, drive, payments so a typical custom-app developer doesn't see Frappe-org noise on day one. Remove the rows you actively contribute to (ERPNext core, HRMS, etc.). The "Issues found" stat card shows the kept count plus a "N findings hidden" note, so the total stays honest.

Patterns and users to exclude from instrumentation. Matches against request path / job kwargs / session user. The profiler's own admin endpoints are always skipped these settings extend the built-in skip list.

fields.description: One URL prefix per line. Any request whose path starts with one of these is never profiled, even during an active session. Handy for health-check endpoints, polling APIs and the like. Lines starting with # are treated as comments. Example: /api/method/ping
fields.label: Skip Request Paths

fields.description: One user email per line. Requests or jobs running as any of these users are never profiled. Handy for leaving out system or bot users such as the scheduler. Lines starting with # are treated as comments.
fields.label: Skip Users

fields.options: Optimus redacts sensitive values at capture time passwords, API keys, tokens, CSRF, cookies and authorization headers never reach Redis or the persisted report. Defaults cover 12 canonical patterns. Add domain-specific names below (one per line) to extend redaction; defaults are never removed. Substring match, case-insensitive. Lines starting with # are comments.

fields.label: Sensitive SQL Columns
fields.description: Extra database column names whose values should be hidden. When one of these appears in a query filter, its value is replaced with '<REDACTED>'. One name per line. Example: recovery_code, bank_account, otp_seed.

fields.label: Sensitive Form / Header Keys
fields.description: Extra form-field or request-header names whose values should be hidden. Each match is replaced with '<REDACTED:keyname>'. One name per line. Example: x-customer-id, recovery_code.

fields.options:
Long-running flows (bulk inserts, complex Submit chains) can exceed the per-recording query cap during analyze-time enrichment each query needs an EXPLAIN round-trip, so very high counts would exceed RQ's job timeout. When capped, the report covers the first N queries and the rest are truncated; a red banner at the top of the report surfaces the truncation so you know the analysis is partial.

Default: 2000 comfortable for most flows. Raise to 5000 or 10000 for flows that legitimately touch more rows (e.g. Manufacturing Plan Submit creating 100+ child orders). Analyze-time cost scales roughly linearly with this value.

fields.description: Each recording enriches at most this many queries with the full treatment (tidy formatting, a query plan and normalization). Anything past the limit is dropped with a warning. Keep it sensible, since each query adds one database round-trip. Set it to 0 for no limit, which enriches every query but makes analyze time grow with the number of queries, so save that for deep investigations. Reference values: Strict: 0  ·  Recommended: 2000  ·  Relaxed: 1000.
fields.label: Max Queries per Recording

fields.description: The profiler samples what your code is doing this often, in milliseconds. A smaller number captures more detail but adds more overhead; a larger number is lighter but coarser. 1ms suits most cases, raise it to 5-10ms when profiling on a busy production-like site. It cannot go below 0.1ms. Reference values: Strict: 0.5  ·  Recommended: 1.0  ·  Relaxed: 5.0.
fields.label: Sampler Interval (ms)

fields.description: When ticked, the report's "Time spent per database table" section hides Frappe's own internal tables (things like tabDocType, tabDocField, tabSingles, tabRole and the information_schema tables) that every request touches through the framework and that you cannot act on. A short "(N tables hidden)" note takes their place. The other sections (top queries, per-action drill-down, full recordings) are not affected. Untick to see every table.
fields.label: Hide framework / internal database tables in the breakdown

fields.description: The analyze step waits this many seconds (capped at 300) for the background jobs your flow started to finish before it builds the report. Every such job is listed in the report's "Background jobs" section with its status. A job still going when the wait runs out is shown as "Running", so click Retry Analyze once it finishes to pull in its data. Use 0 to skip waiting. On a single-worker bench the analyze step steps aside between checks so those jobs can actually run. If the scheduler is off or no worker is available, the wait is skipped. Reference values: Strict: 300  ·  Recommended: 300  ·  Relaxed: 60.
fields.label: Wait for Background Jobs (seconds)

fields.options: These thresholds affect how Optimus renders the report they don't change what's captured or analyzed.

fields.description: Hide actions shorter than this many milliseconds from the per-action breakdown in the report. Use 0 to show everything. Handy for cutting clutter when a flow fires lots of tiny background polls. Reference values: Strict: 1  ·  Recommended: 0  ·  Relaxed: 50.
fields.label: Min Action Duration to Show (ms)

fields.description: Show any duration above this many milliseconds in seconds instead. For example, with the default of 1000, 5234ms shows as 5.23s while 800ms stays as 800ms. Set it to 0 to turn this off and keep every duration in milliseconds. Reference values: Strict: 500  ·  Recommended: 1000  ·  Relaxed: 99999999.
fields.label: Render durations in seconds above (ms)

fields.options: Pick a preset to set every tunable threshold across Optimus in one move analyzer thresholds (the original nine), capture knobs (max queries / sampler interval / background-job wait), retention, display filters, Phase-2 defaults and the AI auto-suggest cap. Strict catches more (more findings, more noise) and keeps data longer; Relaxed catches less and prunes faster; Recommended is the shipped default and automatically tracks future tuning. Choose Custom to edit the individual fields yourself they stay locked under the named presets.

fields.description: A preset for how sensitive the detection thresholds below should be. The named presets (Strict, Recommended, Relaxed) set those thresholds for you and keep the individual fields read-only. Recommended follows the shipped defaults across upgrades. Switch to Custom to set the thresholds by hand.
fields.label: Sensitivity Profile

fields.options: How many identical calls from the same callsite qualify as a Redundant Call finding and how many identical queries from the same callsite qualify as an N+1 finding. Lower = more sensitive = more findings; higher = fewer findings but less noise.

fields.description: The same document must be loaded this many times from the same spot in the code before it is flagged as a Redundant Call. Reference values: Strict: 3  ·  Recommended: 5  ·  Relaxed: 10.
fields.label: Redundant get_doc Threshold

fields.description: The same cache key must be looked up this many times from the same spot in the code before it is flagged as a Redundant Call. Cache lookups are not timed one by one, so small loops look just like normal framework background noise. 50 lines up with the high-severity threshold and cuts out the 0ms noise. Reference values: Strict: 20  ·  Recommended: 50  ·  Relaxed: 100.
fields.label: Redundant Cache Lookup Threshold

fields.description: The same permission check must run this many times from the same spot in the code before it is flagged as a Redundant Call. Reference values: Strict: 5  ·  Recommended: 10  ·  Relaxed: 25.
fields.label: Redundant Permission Check Threshold

fields.description: The same query must run this many times from the same spot in the code before it is flagged as an N+1 Query. Reference values: Strict: 5  ·  Recommended: 10  ·  Relaxed: 25.
fields.label: N+1 Minimum Occurrences

fields.options: Tune what counts as a high-severity finding. Sites with intentionally slow analytical flows (legitimate full-table scans, large reports) want higher numbers to suppress false positives; sites with strict latency budgets want lower numbers to surface anything borderline.

fields.description: A single SQL query that takes longer than this many milliseconds is flagged as a Slow Query. The default is 200ms; anything under that is usually fine for a single query. Reference values: Strict: 100  ·  Recommended: 200  ·  Relaxed: 500.
fields.label: Slow Query Threshold (ms)

fields.description: The Slow Hot Path threshold, as a percentage of the action's total time. A branch of the call tree qualifies when it uses at least this percentage of the time and also at least the minimum milliseconds set below. The default is 25% with a 200ms minimum. Reference values: Strict: 15  ·  Recommended: 25  ·  Relaxed: 40.
fields.label: Slow Hot Path Threshold (% of action wall time)

fields.description: The smallest absolute time a Slow Hot Path must take. A branch of the call tree qualifies only when it meets both the percentage above and at least this many milliseconds. Reference values: Strict: 100  ·  Recommended: 200  ·  Relaxed: 500.
fields.label: Slow Hot Path Minimum (ms)

fields.description: For Phase 2 line profiling: a single line is flagged as High severity when it uses at least this percentage of its function's total time and also at least the minimum milliseconds below. The default is 50% with a 100ms minimum. Reference values: Strict: 35  ·  Recommended: 50  ·  Relaxed: 70.
fields.label: Hot Line High Severity (% of function time)

fields.description: The smallest absolute time a single line must take to be flagged as High severity in Phase 2 line profiling. Reference values: Strict: 50  ·  Recommended: 100  ·  Relaxed: 250.
fields.label: Hot Line High Severity Min (ms)

fields.options: Defaults for the phase-2 line-profile pass. The picker dialog still lets the user override these per run.

fields.description: Each session keeps at most this many Phase 2 runs in full. Once there are more, the oldest run's full results are moved to a private file and only its summary row stays on the record. Set it to 0 for no limit, but keep an eye on record size for heavy users. Reference values: Strict: 0  ·  Recommended: 10  ·  Relaxed: 5.
fields.label: Phase 2: Max Runs per Session

fields.description: When ticked, the 'Auto-expand hot chain' box in the picker starts already checked. Auto-expand follows each suggested pick down the Phase 1 call tree so the whole hot chain gets profiled in one go.
fields.label: Phase 2: Default Auto-Expand Hot Chain

fields.description: Auto-expand follows into the call tree at most this many levels from a suggested pick. Set it to 0 for unlimited depth, which walks all the way to the leaves (pair it with an auto-expand minimum of 0 for the deepest possible profiling). Reference values: Strict: 0  ·  Recommended: 10  ·  Relaxed: 5.
fields.label: Auto-Expand: Max Depth

fields.description: Auto-expand stops going deeper once the next-hottest child takes less than this many milliseconds. A lower value follows further into smaller hot spots; a higher value stops sooner and profiles fewer functions. Set it to 0 to follow into every measurable child (no minimum). Reference values: Strict: 10  ·  Recommended: 50  ·  Relaxed: 100.
fields.label: Auto-Expand: Minimum Child Time (ms)

fields.options: When enabled, a Suggest a fix (AI) button appears on the Optimus Session form. Clicking it sends the selected finding's context finding type, callsite, a window of surrounding source code, the normalized SQL and EXPLAIN row to the configured LLM and stores the returned fix on the finding (it also shows up in the regenerated HTML report). This sends code and queries to your chosen provider. Point Base URL at a local model (Ollama / LM Studio / vLLM) to keep everything on-box. Read the full data-flow documentation what's sent, what isn't and step-by-step local-LLM recipes.

fields.description: The master on/off switch for AI fix suggestions. Off by default.
fields.label: Enable AI Fix Suggestions

fields.description: This picks the AI provider's wire format. "OpenAI-compatible" needs a Base URL and a Model. Use it for Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter, Together, Groq and similar.
fields.label: Provider

fields.description: The base address of your OpenAI-compatible endpoint (include /v1). For example http://localhost:11434/v1 (Ollama), http://localhost:1234/v1 (LM Studio) or https://openrouter.ai/api/v1. Hosted providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi) use their own built-in address, so this box is hidden for them.
fields.label: Base URL

fields.description: Leave this blank to use the provider's default model. Examples: claude-sonnet-4-6 (Anthropic), gpt-4.1-mini (OpenAI), kimi-k2-0905-preview (Kimi) or the name of your local model.
fields.label: Model

fields.description: The provider's API key, if it needs one. Stored encrypted for this site. Most local endpoints (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) do not need a key; hosted ones (OpenAI, Anthropic, Kimi, OpenRouter, Together, Groq) do.
fields.label: API Key

fields.description: Choose which parts of the report are allowed to use the AI. Turning one off disables it completely: that part is never generated automatically, its buttons on the session form are hidden, the API turns down requests for it and re-rendered reports leave it out.
fields.label: Use the LLM for

fields.description: When off, findings get no AI-suggested fix: nothing is generated during analyze, the "Suggest a fix (AI)", "Generate AI fixes" and "Re-evaluate AI fixes" buttons are hidden, the API turns down requests and re-rendered reports leave out the AI-fix block.
fields.label: Fix suggestions on findings

fields.description: When off, there is no "Index advice (AI)" block in the "Time spent per database table" section: nothing is generated automatically, the "Suggest an index (AI)" button is hidden, the API turns down requests and re-rendered reports leave it out.
fields.label: Index recommendations (DB-tables breakdown)

fields.description: When ticked, the AI rewrites each session's auto-generated "Steps to Reproduce" note into a friendly, readable flow (if the AI call fails, the note falls back to the plain list of captured actions; the per-action breakdown lists them either way). When off, the note stays as the plain action list, the "Humanize Steps (AI)" button is hidden and the API turns down requests. An older session that was already humanized keeps its note until it is re-analyzed.
fields.label: Humanized "Steps to Reproduce"

fields.description: When ticked, analyze automatically asks the AI for a fix on every eligible finding, so the suggestions are already in the report with no need to click "Suggest a fix (AI)" for each one. This spends AI tokens (and a little extra analyze time) on every session that is analyzed, so keep it off unless you want suggestions built in by default.
fields.label: Suggest AI fixes in the report by default

fields.description: Analyze adds an automatic suggestion to at most this many findings per session, taking the highest-severity, highest-impact ones first. Use 0 for every eligible finding, which can be slow and costly on big sessions. Reference values: Strict: 0  ·  Recommended: 5  ·  Relaxed: 3.
fields.label: Max auto-suggested findings per session

fields.options: Per-type opt-out and the local-LLM timeout. The exclusion list is the only way (short of disabling AI entirely) to keep a specific finding category from ever being built into a payload useful when a particular type embeds business logic you don't want shared with a hosted provider. The timeout knob exists for local LLMs: hosted providers usually answer in seconds, but a cold-start ollama / vLLM run can take well over a minute on first call.

fields.description: One finding type per line. These types are skipped by both automatic and on-demand AI suggestions (no request is ever built for them). Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Lines starting with '#' are comments. Use the official names: Filesort, Framework N+1, Full Table Scan, Hot Line, Low Filter Ratio, Missing Index, N+1 Query, Redundant Call, Slow Query, Temporary Table.
fields.label: Excluded finding types

fields.description: Optimus waits this many seconds for an outbound AI call before giving up. The default of 60s suits hosted providers (Anthropic and OpenAI usually reply in 2 to 10s). Local models (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) can take longer than 60s for the first token on a cold start, so start at 180 and lower it once you know your warm-call times. Kept within 10 to 600s.
fields.label: Request timeout (seconds)
